key_insight: The hard-sphere Boltzmann collision hierarchy can be generated from a single primitive rank-two stress-production vertex, S, rather than from many independent collision laws.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the apparent complexity of collision modeling and could simplify kinetic-based surrogates for rarefied-gas and high-speed flow simulation.
method: Proved that every polynomial collision vertex is derived from S via universal differential and tensor operations.
Showed that conventional collisional brackets follow by differentiation from the same primitive law.
Separated hard-sphere-specific physics from universal algebraic structure in the hierarchy.
evidence_signal: A blind eighth-order test in a Mach-5 shock matched independent collision sampling and amplified a weak kinetic precursor.
watch_item: The result is mathematically powerful, but practical use may depend on stable high-order differentiation and faithful numerical realization of the vertex-based construction.
paper_title: One vertex generates the hard-sphere Boltzmann collision hierarchy
